title: No Two People Age in the Same Way - Nautilus

text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementGeneticsNo Two People Age in the Same WayAt least at the molecular levelJCBy Jake Currie1:00 PM CDT on September 3, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleAs Tolstoy wrote in Anna Karenina, “All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.” The same can be said about how we age. We all may start out relatively healthy, but as time passes, different things start to break down inside different people, and the result is our very own unique aging journey. According to a comprehensive new study published in Science, the individuality of aging is especially conspicuous at the molecular level.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoFor eight years, an international team of scientists led by researchers at King’s College London followed a group of 335 healthy women from the U.K.. During that time, the team took blood samples to measure expression changes in 16,000 genes as well as the levels of hundreds of metabolites. The results were some of the most detailed long-term studies of transcriptomics and metabolomics related to aging to date. Read more: “How Our Perceptions of Aging Can Affect Our Social Lives”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
